Auburn University researchers in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and aquaculture will receive nearly $1.3 million in research grants, Gov. Kay Ivey announced this week. The funding is part of a combined $8.1 million investment from the Alabama Research and Development Enhancement Fund administered by the Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA).

Three Auburn projects were included among the grants, which are being issued to provide practical solutions to emerging challenges and to promote economic growth in the region:

The projects align with Auburn's Strategic Plan 2035 goals for doubling its research activity through impactful scholarly work that enhances economic prosperity and solves problems through collaborative team science.

"ADECA's latest investment in Auburn's research confirms the university's position as a trusted partner in improving quality of life for the citizens of Alabama," said Steve Taylor, senior vice president for research and economic development. "These funds will be used to leverage Auburn researchers' expertise in AI technology development and chemical engineering processes to make AI tools easier to use, to enhance community safety and to help farmers ensure a cost-effective agricultural supply chain."

The Auburn research projects are expected to run for two years. Learn more about the Alabama Research and Development Enhancement Fund grants via ADECA's announcement.
